地点只用于右侧天空图；两图共用下方 UTC 时刻，不改原实验台。: This location applies only to the sky reference. Both views share the UTC control below; the main lab is unchanged.
北纬、东经为正。天空位置含地平视差，未计大气折射；地平线下的天体也会注明。: North latitude and east longitude are positive. Sky positions include topocentric parallax but exclude atmospheric refraction. Bodies below the horizon are identified.
位置由 Astronomy Engine 计算，轨道是星历采样的路径。日心距离采: Positions come from Astronomy Engine; orbit guides sample the ephemeris. Heliocentric distances use a power-law display compression, while body sizes are enlarged separately. The Sun–Earth–Moon view uses a separate Earth–Moon distance scale. Screen sizes and distances are not to physical scale.
日地月视图的箭头指向远处太阳，照明使用平行光；外部相机所见月面不等同于地球观测月: In the Sun–Earth–Moon view, the arrow points toward the distant Sun and sunlight is parallel. The Moon seen from the external camera is not the phase seen from Earth; its geocentric illuminated fraction is calculated separately. Surface and cloud textures are illustrative, not images for the selected date. Earth's rotation and axis follow UTC; other bodies' orientations are illustrative. Eclipses and local rise/set events are not simulated here.
日期轴连续改变 UTC 时刻；日历选择定位当天12:00 UTC。旋转和缩放只改: The date slider changes UTC continuously; selecting a calendar date sets 12:00 UTC. Rotation and zoom change only the camera, not physical positions. This page has its own state, so your main lab settings are preserved.
“参照”共用同一 UTC 时刻：空间俯视是固定黄道平面的投影，本地天空是所选地点: Reference views share the same UTC. The top view projects onto the fixed ecliptic plane; the local sky shows azimuth and altitude at the selected location. These 2D views stay fixed as the 3D camera rotates, distinguishing spatial motion from apparent sky motion.
星等控制显示明暗，B−V色指数近似恒星颜色；星点大小与柔光为显示处理。背景不做大: Magnitude controls displayed brightness, and B−V approximates star color. Point sizes and glow are display effects. The background excludes atmospheric scintillation, proper motion, annual parallax, and horizon obstruction; it is not a precision observing chart.

Except for the Moon and the four Galilean moons, orbits are approximated from JPL mean elements. Coverage follows the available orbit table; not every newly discovered object has orbital data. Nebula backgrounds are enlarged observational images, not their actual angular sizes or naked-eye views.
